Author's Note

Laura Monsalvatge, PhD is an Assistant Teaching Professor of Early Childhood Education in FIU’s Department of Teaching and Learning. She regularly teaches Family Literacy and the Young Child (EEC 3400) and Children’s Literature (LAE4405)—both Global Learning–designated courses that examine how cultures around the world approach education, family reading practices, and storytelling.

With more than 25 years of experience working with and teaching about young children, Dr. Monsalvatge’s scholarship and teacher-education practice center on: early childhood education; infant and toddler learning; nature and outdoor spaces for young children; and social-emotional development. Her pedagogy foregrounds equity and the transformative power of schooling, guided by a favorite line from Kofi Annan: “Literacy is… the road to human progress and the means through which every man, woman and child can realize his or her full potential.”

At FIU, she is recognized among Global Learning faculty for advancing high-impact, globally minded teaching.

She has presented her work at local, national, and international conferences and mentors preservice teachers in designing culturally responsive, play-rich, and nature-based literacy experiences for young learners.

Introduction

When you open this course, you won’t just see a syllabus—you will enter a structured, embedded storybook. Each module functions as a chapter that guides you through central questions in children’s literature using narrative-driven, immersive constructivism techniques. The format is approachable by design, but the work is rigorous: you will interrogate texts, synthesize research, and design evidence-based instructional moves.

Across the chapters, you will examine core genres and literary elements while analyzing how high-quality texts support language, cognitive, social, and emotional development. You will evaluate books for representation, developmental appropriateness, and instructional utility; practice differentiating for diverse learners; and consider how literature fosters empathy and global understanding. In short, you will learn to read like a scholar and select like a teacher.

By the end of the term, you will have an annotated, developmentally aligned text set, a portfolio of classroom-ready mini-lessons and assessments, and a professional rationale that connects research on children’s literature to equitable practice. You will leave prepared to justify book choices, design engaging reading experiences, and use narrative to advance clear learning goals.

Expect an active, collaborative environment. You will produce concise analytic memos, critique peers’ plans, and translate theory into practice through the storybook activities. The goal is not novelty for its own sake; it is to leverage an immersive format to help you think critically, teach thoughtfully, and use children’s literature as a powerful instrument for learning and inclusion.

Getting Started

When you first open our course in Canvas, start with Course Navigation → Simple Syllabus. Read it carefully, and jot down the key dates, major assignments, and any technology you’ll need, then add those deadlines to your calendar.

Next, visit the Student Resources module. Think of it as your safety net: tech help, library links, accessibility services, writing support, and Global Learning. Bookmark what you’re likely to use so you’re not hunting for it later.

From there, head into Module 0. Work through each item in order—run the tech checks, try the short tool walk-throughs, and complete the quick acknowledgments so nothing blocks you later.

Once that’s done, step into Module 1 and post your introduction. Share who you are, what you hope to learn, and a children’s book or author that matters to you. We’re building a thoughtful community here, and your voice belongs in it.

If anything feels confusing or a tool doesn’t cooperate, use the Need Help options—Chat, Phone, Walk-In, or Message Your Instructor.

By the end of this first visit, you’ll have the syllabus in hand, resources at your fingertips, Module 0 finished, and your introduction in Module 1—ready to settle in and learn.
